target_customer: Hardware engineering teams, robotics and drone companies and defense electronics teams needing US-made circuit boards quickly
problem: Domestic circuit board manufacturing is slow and expensive, and over half of lead time goes to quoting, DFM review and part sourcing rather than manufacturing.
business_model: Manufacturing service: instant quote, sourced BOM and assembled boards routed to US fab and assembly partners
product_category: Electronics manufacturing (PCB fabrication and assembly orchestration)

founders.name: Johnny Doyle
education: Trinity College Dublin, Engineering with Management (dropped out)
previous_startups: Syncra (office energy management idea they first applied to YC with)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he previously shipped IoT building management systems.

founders.name: Will Carkner
founders.background_notes: Electrical engineer on hydrogen battery systems at Lumindt, built the PCB testing pipeline there per YC page.

competitors.name: CircuitHub
competitors.what: Automated electronics manufacturing, robot factory called The Grid in Massachusetts
competitors.traction_then: claims PCBs built about twice as fast as Shenzhen
competitors.funding_then: raised $28M led by Plural in May 2026

competitors.name: FlashPCB
competitors.what: US prototyping service using software and AI, aims to assemble boards in 3 days

technical_complexity.rationale: Quoting, DFM review and sourcing automation is standard software with hard supply chain integration; manufacturing is done by partners, so no fab R&D is needed.

defensibility.rationale: Orchestrating existing fabs and assemblers is copyable, and CircuitHub was already automating the same pain with far more capital. Partner relationships and ITAR-safe US routing are the only edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. CircuitHub raised $28M weeks before the batch to attack the same wedge.

market_need_then: Reshoring and defense demand: a trade article in the results says domestic fabricators fell from over 2,000 to around 145, and the founders say they spent 90 percent of their time assembling boards by hand before building the service.

branding.domain_note: Uses provenmetal.com exact match; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: Industrial manufacturing site with spec lists
identity.voice_and_tone: Short confident declarative copy; headline We build circuit boards fast; closes with America builds again.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post and Trinity College news item; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests durable metal manufacturing and fits the reshoring message, but it is brand new and only launch coverage exists.

pivots.from: Syncra, an office energy management project the founders first applied to YC with
pivots.why: Third party coverage says YC felt the first idea was not ambitious enough; exact date not stated.

outcome_analysis: ProvenMetal is a Summer 2026 YC company that pivoted from an energy management idea to fast US-made circuit boards. It is too early for an outcome. The pain is real and defense and reshoring tailwinds help, but CircuitHub is well funded and the service depends on partner fabs, so defensibility rests on speed and relationships.
notes: VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed in June 2026 and the TCD-linked coverage mentions YC's $500K standard package; this is only one aggregator plus the standard YC deal, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. One aggregator (sesamedisk) describes benchtop X-ray inspection, which conflicts with all other sources and is ignored. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Completeness pass: the $500K June 2026 round is recorded from VCBacked, a single database (CB Insights calls it a convertible note, a YC directory calls it seed); likely the YC standard package. Irish Times and Trinity College Dublin coverage confirm YC acceptance but give no round terms.
